name: discovery-listing
comment_engines: Next 14 requires >=18.17. The upload routes used to need >=20 for the File global; they no longer do (src/lib/upload.ts), so 18.17 is the real floor. Production runs 18.19.

scripts.comment_build: NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD stamps the commit into the bundle. Without it there is no way to tell a deployed build from a stale one — a debug endpoint answered in an OLD response shape and it took a round trip to work out the server had simply not been rebuilt. `|| echo unknown` so a tarball deploy with no .git still builds.
scripts.build: NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown) next build
scripts.comment_deploy: THE deploy command, and the only one to type on the server. Derives the repo root from its own location (no path to fill in), refuses a dirty tree, fast-forwards only, and then DECIDES FROM THE DIFF what to rebuild and restart: bot/ -> the ecosystem file (both bots), tradebot/ -> its own process, shared/ -> all three, anything else -> the web app. A bot-only change therefore pays no Next build. It verifies every process afterwards by reading the commit it reports (the web app from /api/tokens, the bots from their [boot] build line) -- a stale process answers 200 and starts cleanly, which is why neither is the check. --with-bots forces the bot suite on; --all forces everything; with nothing to pull it verifies and restarts nothing, which makes it the 'what is actually running?' command too.
scripts.comment_deploy_all: Same deploy, but rebuild and restart EVERY process whatever the diff says. For a box whose state is in doubt, or after a hand-edit was reverted.
scripts.comment_test_pons: The Pons v2 provider reads contracts, not an HTTP API, so its tests drive a FAKE JSON-RPC node: keccak/ABI vectors, bonding-curve and Uniswap V4 price math, the rolling log window and the announce-once guarantee. No network, no box required.
scripts.comment_pons_check: The feed renders three independent failures identically as null — the factory logs, the eth_calls on the curve and the token, and GeckoTerminal's reference price. This asks each separately ON THE BOX, because whether an RPC honours a 27-call batch and whether GT answers this IP are properties of the server today, not of the code.
scripts.comment_chart_check: Whether an upstream ANSWERS is a property of the server's egress today, not of the code — the rule raid:check, launchpads:check and fonts:check all state. This one says it about a request shape that is a GUESS: DexScreener publishes no documented OHLCV endpoint, so a red line here is a .env fix (DS_CHART_API / DS_CHART_PATH / DS_CHART_BARS_KEY) rather than a deploy. It drives the provider's real entry points, prints the build stamp, and exits non-zero only when NEITHER source can draw.
scripts.comment_firstpaint: Does the page ARRIVE with the board in it, and is anything third-party blocking it? Measured against the running server. It retries, because a process that has just booted legitimately ships the shell rather than hang on a cold market read — the one-liner that preceded this printed 0 for exactly that reason, seconds after a pm2 restart, and read as a broken deploy.
scripts.comment_ds_probe: chart:check reports that the guessed DexScreener candle shape failed and then tells the operator to read the real one out of a browser's DevTools. The box is not a browser — but it can read the browser's code. This resolves the pair through the documented api. host, greps dexscreener.com's own JS bundle for the datafeed host and path, probes each candidate with dsChart's real headers, and prints the .env lines for whatever answers with bars. A wrong guess stays a .env line, never a deploy.
scripts.comment_ds_apply: The same probe, applying what it finds: it upserts DS_CHART_API/PATH/QUERY into .env.local (after a backup) instead of printing them for a human to paste. Opt-in via --write because a probe that edits an operator's environment unasked is not a probe.
scripts.comment_chart_preview: The chart panel is judged by LOOKING at it — a clipped axis stamp and a smeared phone window both passed the unit tests. Needs a running server; stubs the upstreams in the browser so it works with no egress.
scripts.comment_logos_check: Which listed tokens would draw a monogram, and WHICH of the three causes it is: the row lost its logo, the uploaded file is gone, or our own proxy refuses a working url. Drives the running server and pulls each logo through the same /api/logo the browser uses — whether a CDN answers is a property of this box's egress today. Non-zero when any row would draw a monogram.
scripts.comment_market_check: Three failures render identically as a chain of $0 rows: GT has nothing for the tokens, GT is refusing this box, or the site pipeline is broken. This drives the RUNNING server's /api/tokens AND GeckoTerminal directly with the site's own request shape, and says which one broke. Measured on the box because whether GT answers is a property of this server's egress today.
